title: Dedicated capacity acceptance profiles and realistic prober for throughput/SLO validation
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build a repeatable, customer-facing acceptance kit that validates Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaling policies using realistic, workload-shaped traffic. This ticket defines acceptance profiles, the realistic prober harness, statistical benchmarking methodology, and automated customer acceptance tests (CATs) for Dedicated pool certification.

Goals:
- Define 5 canonical acceptance profiles (baseline steady, sustained high, burst+tail, cold-start-heavy, degraded-fallback) that map to customer SLAs and sales commitments.
- Implement a 'realistic prober' traffic generator that can replay recorded production traces, synthesize mixed batch sizes, and exercise KV cache warmup semantics.
- Establish benchmarking methodology: warmup phases, steady-state window, sample size targets, and P50/P95/P99/token throughput metrics with confidence intervals.
- Produce automated CATs that run post-deploy and produce a human-readable acceptance report + machine-readable artifact for pipelines.

Scope and approach:
- Traffic library: capture anonymized trace samples from hosted customers and internal load labs; implement scenario templates (prompt length distribution, role/chat vs. single-turn, embedding vs. generation).
- Harness components: controller (orchestration), prober workers (multithreaded), KV-warmup module, model-variant selector (FP16/quantized), and result aggregator.
- Autoscaling probes: run step-up/down experiments to validate configured cooldowns, max pods, and graceful degradation policies; include a chaos probe that kills a node and verifies fallback routing.
- Metrics and analysis: collect per-token latency histograms, request-level success/failure, GPU utilization, queue lengths, and model-switch events. Reporting includes CSV export and Grafana dashboard snapshot.

Acceptance criteria (customer-facing):
- For the baseline profile, sustained 60-minute run: measured throughput within +/-5% of contract target and P95 latency below SLA target.
- Burst profile: 30s spike to 3x baseline should not exceed the configured cold-start window and should keep error rate <0.5%.
- Autoscaler validation: when load increases above scale-up threshold, additional capacity should appear within configured cooldown + 30s variance and capacity should not oscillate.
- Degraded fallback: when primary model variant is unavailable, routing to a lower-cost/latency-compatible variant must maintain a defined QoS floor and report the switch in acceptance artifacts.

Deliverables:
- Realistic prober code in repo: infra/throughput-prober (CLI + job templates).
- Scenario library of JSON profiles and anonymized trace examples.
- Confluence playbook: "Dedicated Capacity Acceptance Cookbook" with runbook steps and interpretation guidance.
- Automated GitHub Action that runs CATs against canary clusters and uploads results to the release artifacts.

Risks & mitigations:
- High variance from synthetic traffic: mitigate by bootstrapping from production traces and running multiple iterations to compute confidence intervals.
- KV cache sensitivity: include explicit warmup and cache-scrubbing steps in profiles.
- Customer data sensitivity: use anonymized/pseudonymized prompt corpus and exclude PII traces. Security review flagged (see security_review_required).

Open questions:
- Do sales/legal teams want a signed acceptance SLA template for customers to opt into CAT-based certification? (Action: loop in Sarah O'Neill)
- Thresholds for "QoS floor" when falling back to quantized variants — propose: 80% of baseline throughput and P95 latency <= 2x SLA.

Next steps (short term):
- Spike: implement trace replay adapter + KV warmup flow (owner: Marcus) by 2026-03-12.
- Draft profile definitions and run the first baseline + burst runs in the load lab by 2026-03-16.
- Create initial Grafana dashboard and acceptance report template by 2026-03-18.
comments: 2026-03-11: Spike done — trace replay adapter can ingest newline-delimited JSON traces exported from prod-loader. Observed heavy tail in prompt length distribution (very long outliers).
2026-03-12: Discovered KV cache warmup adds ~8% throughput delta for steady-state if not prewarmed; added KV-warmup module to harness.
2026-03-13: Ran initial baseline run in the lab (30m): throughput target missed by 7% due to serialization bottleneck in the prober. Marcus to prototype parallelized sender.
2026-03-13: Reached out to Sarah O'Neill (sales) for customer-facing SLA language. Received tentative approval to offer CAT certification as an add-on.
